extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of digital media, communication, and meme studies (researchers analyzing internet memes)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply a memetic analytical framework to digital memes by examining their content, form, and stance, plus related properties that drive circulation, meaning, and social effects across platforms. Useful for coding, qualitative analysis, and theorizing memetic phenomena in digital culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content (memetic dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dimension of 'content' refers to the kinds of ideas, messages, or feelings that are conveyed within a meme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding or analyzing memes, identify the themes, messages, emotions, narratives or statements the meme communicates (e.g., political critique, identity markers, jokes). Use content comparisons across clustered examples to reevaluate elements constitutive to a meme, trend, style, or genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form (memetic dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'form' dimension confronts the audio, visual, and textual or symbolic means through which a meme takes shape, as well as the genre-related patterning thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the media affordances (images, video, audio, text overlays, macros, templates), genre conventions (image macros, lip-sync vids), and formal templates a meme uses. Record and compare formal elements across instances to establish prototypical formal features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stance (memetic dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'stance' dimension addresses the position that a creator of memetic content takes toward both the discourses and formats that are more generally associated with a specific meme or trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the creator's position is ironic, sincere, mocking, supportive, parodic, etc., and how that orientation interacts with content and form. Stance is dialogic and indexes broader sociocultural contexts; examine public positioning and interactional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitional criteria for an Internet meme
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes are cultural information/items that pass from person to person, reproduced by imitation (replication/remix), and diffused through competition and selection; they often 'share common characteristics of content, form, and/or stance,' are created with awareness of each other, and are circulated, imitated, and transformed via the Internet by multiple users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitional tests to decide whether a digital item qualifies as a meme: presence of imitation/remix potential, multimodal templateness, repeatability across users, and observable circulation dynamics. Examples (e.g., 'Leave Britney Alone') can demonstrate replication and remix processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Features driving virality
rubrics_metrics.description: Four primary features commonly attributed to memes' viral spread: affectiveness, interactivity, variability, and collectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analysis, assess how a meme elicits emotion (affectiveness), allows or invites user participation/interaction (interactivity), supports variation and remix (variability), and functions as a shared, collective practice (collectiveness). These features help explain propagation and reception differences across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodality (memes as multimodal artefacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes are multimodal artefacts that combine text, image, audio, gesture, and intertextual cues to produce compressed forms of social commentary, affective positioning, and cultural evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to how visual elements anchor textual meaning, how timing/gesture and audio contribute to reading, and how semiotic compression works. Treat memes as multimodal packages rather than purely visual or verbal items in coding and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform affordances and governance shape meme circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation systems, recommendation infrastructures, and other platform affordances actively shape visibility, participation, and cultural circulation rather than merely hosting memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider algorithmic curation, moderation policies, 'use this sound' features, and platform-specific formal constraints (video length, templates) when analyzing reach, mutation, and meaning. Platform ecology is a critical variable in memetic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communities of practice and contextual protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Memetic meaning is often governed by implicit or explicit community protocols: who follows the meme, who understands it, and which rules/expectations determine appropriate reuse and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the in-group knowledge required to decode a meme, membership practices, and how exclusion/inclusion operate. Note that memetic discourse can exclude those who do not follow central protocols of content, form, and stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic functions: instrumental vs. situational
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes perform functions that can be instrumental (purposeful advocacy, marketing, identity work) or situational (ephemeral reactions tied to specific events), depending on context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify meme instances by function: are they intended as long-term identity markers or immediate situational commentary? This guides sampling and interpretation of memetic roles in social/political processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifecycle dynamics: mutation, repackaging, snowcloning, rise and decay
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes undergo processes of mutation ('mutation'/'repackaging'), snowcloning, and a life cycle that includes emergence, growth, conventionalization, and decline/decay (loss of multimodality or precedent potential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace a meme's transformations over time and map typical stages; identify how templates are adapted, which variations succeed, and when a meme loses traction or multimodal integrity. Use lifecycle analysis to explain longevity and conventionalisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic practices (engagement types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memetic engagements include practices such as gaining knowledge about memes, spreading memes, and creating memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying audiences or producers, measure and code behaviors: consumption/curation, sharing/propagation acts, and original creation/remix. These practices are analytical variables for diffusion and participatory culture studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memes as tools for identity, cohesion, and ideology
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes help form group cohesiveness, portray central themes and social norms, serve as markers of identity, and function as vehicles for ideological expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how memes construct collective identities, normalize discourses, or encode ideological positions (including memetic misogyny or political advertising). Examine narrative roles, archetypes, and mnemonic potential in memory-construction and persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memes as templates for linguistic and creative practice (memetic linguistics / constructional view)
rubrics_metrics.description: In memetic linguistics, linguistic expressions are treated as viral, repeatable, multimodal packages; memes act as constructional templates or form-meaning pairings that can crystallize new conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how particular phraseologies, timing, framing, or visual slots become conventionalized; assess creativity along dimensions of fixedness vs. extension and how form-meaning pairings are expanded through reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memes in marketing/humor: multimodal coordination for persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Humorous and memetic brand communication functions as a persuasive strategy that relies on incongruity-based humor, conceptual blending, and multimodal coordination to amplify engagement and brand identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applied analyses (marketing/advertising), evaluate cognitive mechanisms (incongruity, blending), multimodal alignment (visual/text/audio), and the extent to which memetic humor fosters participatory engagement or extends an ad's conversational life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context dependence and situated interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes are highly context-dependent: their meanings, functions, and valences vary across sociopolitical events, cultural norms, and platform/ecological contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always situate meme analysis in cultural, temporal, and platform contexts; avoid assuming translatability of interpretation across communities or geopolitical settings. Contextual factors can change whether a meme is humorous, hateful, political, or mnemonic.
